executive_summary:
In the window from 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15, ARI3 collected 3,891 raw source records from 78 outlet domains. Final signal evidence was deduplicated so exact mirrors and syndicated or translated versions of the same publication count as one report evidence unit. The editor retained 20 signals. The largest by item count are sneaker (65 items from 18 outlets), denim (25 from 15) and vintage (18 from 13). Sneaker is concentrated, with 29 of its items from two outlets, mostly Nike, Jordan and adidas releases alongside Black Friday sales. Denim spreads across jean colours, cuts and brand news. Vintage appears in film costume design, celebrity dressing and reissues.

Winter footwear, outerwear and colour recur in suede (15 items from 9 outlets), burgundy (13 from 10), leopard and loafer, and leopard leans on holiday products and gift-season coverage. Streetwear and oversized have 9 or 10 items each. The smaller clusters, with 2 to 6 items, are minimalism, bomber, workwear, trench, leather jacket, maximalism, wide-leg, kitten heel, ballet flat, peplum and tailoring. These are patterns in the sources ARI3 collects, which were 89.7% editorial in this window. They do not measure consumer adoption or what people wear.

top_signals.name: sneaker
top_signals.evidence: Release coverage dominates: Nike Air Max, Air Force 1 and Air Jordan releases, Union with Nike, NOCTA, Cactus Plant Flea Market and a new Nike Flyknit, plus collaborations such as Marni with Hoka, ASICS with JUNTAE KIM, Balenciaga with Damien Hirst, HAVEN with Converse, Tyler, the Creator with Converse and BEAMS with Salomon, some in Italian-language GQ Italia headlines (translated). Trend items cover the comeback of Nike's Ovolo and of white 1980s sneakers, retro sneakers and winter sneaker trends, with German-language Vogue Germany headlines (translated). Black Friday sales and GQ features on James Bond's adidas and on owning fewer sneakers complete the set, and a few headlines present flats or other shoes as the alternative.
top_signals.index_note: The signal has 65 items from 18 outlets, editorial 61 and retail 4, on every day of the window. highsnobiety.com contributes 20 items and hypebeast.com 9, so 29 of the 65 come from two outlets. The editor labeled it stable.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Editorial view: sneakers are a stable signal. It's so interesting. Nike dominates the headlines for sure.

limitations: Items are counted as style only when the ARI3 style classifier (frozen v0.0.2) gives a confident yes. On a 150-item prospective holdout of articles published after the classifier was frozen, its accuracy was 0.833, below its pre-registered 0.85 criterion (EXP-003A, H2 not supported). The editor reviews every evidence item used in this report.
In this window, 1,700 of 3,891 items (43.7%) received a not-sure prediction set and were excluded from style-positive counts.

In this window, 89.7% of collected items came from the editorial sector and 95.7% from the editorial group (editorial, trade intelligence and independent criticism). The stored corpus as a whole is 89.3% editorial sector.

The window has 0 items from social platforms, which are not collected, and 1 from resale sources. The report describes the language of the collected sources, not style culture, fashion consumers or the public at large.
Signal interpretation and evidence review are done by one editor.
ARI3 stores each item's headline and feed excerpt, not the full article.
0 of the window's 3891 items were stored before 2026-09-30, so their first-seen times are reconstructed from earlier records, not recorded as they happened.
Seven ambiguous lexicon terms (western, brat, demure, lace, bow, sustainable, glamour) are left out of every count until their uses are checked one by one.

Exact mirrors and syndicated, translated or lightly re-edited versions of the same publication across publisher domains are collapsed to one report evidence unit. The frozen source snapshot retains the raw records.
ai_assistance: ARI3’s deterministic pipeline surfaced candidate signals and bound the report to a frozen evidence snapshot. An AI assistant drafted the executive summary, evidence text, and index notes using only the locked report evidence, including translations of non-English headlines. The editor selected and merged signals, set labels and confidence overrides, pruned evidence, reviewed the drafted text, wrote the editor notes, and approved the final report.
